title: Image overlay
description: A standalone background layer: the shell's needle gradient with a decorative photograph (a real img from its CDN) laid over it in luminosity blend at a whisper of opacity, and the photograph's credit pinned to the bottom-right corner. It takes no children and never assumes the viewport: as the first child of a positioned container it fills that container's full width and height and sits behind the siblings that follow, so it can ground a whole screen, a card or a panel.

anatomy.description: Root div with data-slot="image-overlay": absolute, inset 0, width and height 100%, the needle-400 to needle-700 gradient, isolated, and an inline-size container named image-overlay. Accepts div props; `image` ({ url, creditHref, caption }) swaps the photograph and its credit together. No children.

A decorative img (alt="", async decoding, high fetch priority) covering the ground at z-index -1 inside the isolated root: object-fit cover, luminosity blend, 7.5% opacity, pointer-events none. An element, not a CSS url(): CSS cannot take a URL from a data attribute.
A p with a link to the photograph's page, absolute at the bottom-right: text-2xs, needle-100; bloom-200 on hover, the sidebar's outline step (--nav-outline) on focus.

usage: A background, not a wrapper: it takes no children. Render it as the first child of a positioned container (position: relative or absolute) and put the content after it; it fills the container's full width and height and the later siblings paint above it in DOM order.
It never assumes the viewport. The consumer owns the container, its position and its size: a full screen (min-height 100svh, as the login screen does), a card or a panel all work the same way.
Query narrow layouts against the consumer's container, not the overlay: declare container-type inline-size on the positioned container and write the queries on its children.
A sibling layout that covers the whole ground must give its bare areas pointer-events: none (and its columns pointer-events: auto), or the credit link beneath cannot be clicked.

Pass `image` to change the photograph and the credit changes with it; keep the licence satisfied through the caption. The default is an Unsplash photograph loaded from its CDN, so nothing ships in the bundle.
Keep the blend and the low opacity: luminosity takes the ground's green so the palette stays the only colour source; higher opacity washes out bark-50 copy on the ground.
Do not hide the overlay from assistive tech: the credit is a real link and must stay reachable; the img already carries alt="".
Route code never styles the ground; a surface that needs a different ground is a variant here, not a rule in a route module.
